newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ASC wants single regulator of Australia funds.
newsitem.headline: ASC wants single regulator of Australia funds.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) called on Friday for more coherent regulation of managed funds in Australia but said it did not support the idea of a mega regulator.

"The ASC has supported, in principle, a single regulator approach for managed funds and retail investment advice, but not a mega regulator of the financial system overall," ASC chairman Alan Cameron said in a statement.
The corporate watchdog released the statement with its submission to the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system.

"We believe that while there is scope to develop a more coherent and cost-effective administrative arrangement in the managed funds area, it will not be easy to adopt literally a single regulator for managed funds," Cameron said.
He said the ASC's main task is to provide market integrity and build confidence in the financial markets.
"The ASC believes the current regulation on investment-linked managed funds is not consistent or coherent," the statement said.
Regulation of investment linked managed funds was split, based on whether it was public unit trust or an investment linked life insurance or superannuation product.
The ASC supervised the unit trusts, and the Insurance and Superannuation Commission (ISC) supervised the other products.

Although operational risks were broadly the same, different regulatory standards were applied and this caused problems for the industry by leading to unnecessary costs associated with administration, and may impede competition, the ASC said.
The ASC-preferred proposal was for the ISC reponsibilities for investment-linked superannuation products to be transferred to the ASC.
The current prudential regulation by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) or ISC of capital-backed superannuation promises made by insurance companies or banks would continue.
The ASC said this would take advantge of its expertise in market regulation, and be efficient as it would build upon the ASC's existing national infrastructure and capabilities.
The proposal would also facilitate integration of other managed fund products into the regulatory regime, the ASC said.

Other recommendations included a single regime for investment advice, adopting a consistent framework for disclosure of retail investment products, better coordination of financial services and competition regulation, and supporting a continuing emphasis that regulation of wholesale markets concentrates on ensuring orderly markets and preventing misconduct.
The ASC also recommended some amendments to the Corporations law to enhance its market enforcement ability.

These measures included giving the ASC the power to "protect from liability people who provide investigative assistance or information to the ASC on a voluntary basis and for the ASC to be able to accept enforceable undertakings."
As well, the ASC wanted to change the law so that evidence laws are made uniform throughout Australia.
